verdict: Sweeping the cutpoint over [0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.975, 0.98, 0.99] moves the saturated/non-saturated split away from the reported-in-paper exact 12/12 at every point except cutpoint=0.975 itself (splits: [(16, 8), (12, 12), (12, 12), (12, 12), (12, 12), (12, 12)]), and the ratio of non-saturated to saturated mean Delta_boot ranges 1.64x to 1.76x over the grid (paper's reported 1.6x is the cutpoint=0.975 point in this range). The continuous alternative -- regressing Delta_boot against the selected layer's own naive AUROC with no cutpoint at all -- gives Pearson r=-0.141 (p=0.511), i.e. a not statistically distinguishable from zero negative association between how close to ceiling a cell sits and how large its winner's-curse magnitude is, consistent in DIRECTION with the paper's binary-split finding but not contingent on any specific cutpoint. The exact 12/12 split at 0.975 is therefore a real but cutpoint-specific artifact of that one threshold; the underlying negative relationship between operating point and severity is not, and survives as a continuous, cutpoint-free regression at a similar level of statistical support.
